turns.t: Hello, doctor. I've come about the weight clinic, I think? Or was it the diabetes clinic? Oh, the letter's in my bag somewhere.
The obesity clinic, yes, I've got your referral here. Don't worry about the letter. Tell me what you're hoping for today. ~
To lose weight. I've been trying for years, diets, the gym, all of it, and I put it all back on. I'm up to the highest I've ever been.
How much do you weigh now, as far as you know?
I haven't weighed myself in a month, because the scales scare me. Last time it was a hundred and fourteen.
And how's that affecting you day to day? ~
Knees ache, I get out of breath on the stairs, and I'm tired.
Any chest pain, or breathlessness at rest?
No, nothing at rest. Just on the stairs.
Let me measure you. Stand up, please. ~
Do I have to take my shoes off? ~
Please. I'll measure around your waist, over the belly button.
Is that bad? ~
Your waist measures 112 centimetres, which is in the high-risk range for heart and diabetes problems.
Hmm. I figured. ~
I'm going to be honest with you, and kind: this is a medical condition, not a failure of willpower. There are treatments, including injections, but we start by understanding your whole picture. ~
I've heard about the injections. A neighbour has them. ~
They can work very well for the right people. I'm not starting anything today, because I want your tests first. ~
What tests? ~
I'd like to arrange blood tests, for sugar, cholesterol, liver, kidneys and thyroid, to see what weight is doing to you and whether anything else is contributing.
When? ~
The nurse can take them before you leave. ~
Right. ~
Next, a dietitian will see you, and I'd like you to see them before the next appointment.
A dietitian, not just a leaflet? ~
A proper person, for an hour, to look at what you eat and how. ~
That sounds helpful. ~
For now, keep a food diary for two weeks, everything you eat and drink, honestly, and walk twenty minutes a day.
A diary, I can do that. I'll put it on my phone. ~
Don't change anything yet, just record. ~
Right. ~
Any questions? ~
Yes, where did I put my keys? ~
Check your coat pocket. ~
There they are. Thank you, doctor. ~
